Subject: Latency incidents last week — request for dedicated fallback & credits

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As mentioned, we saw two latency spikes during peak inference windows on 2025-07-15 that impacted our UI responsiveness for roughly 8 minutes total (multiple 500ms+ tail spikes). Our engineering team traced the issue to preemption and queueing behavior on the reserved pool (we're on the Dedicated 12-GPU plan).

Before we escalate to procurement, we want to explore an amendment to our Dedicated SLA that: 1) defines a conditional throughput safeguard (temporary burst reservation/soft headroom) for known seasonal traffic bursts, and 2) spells out crediting for minutes of degraded throughput where preemption or queueing caused tail latency >500ms.

Can Redwood propose a concrete playbook and crediting calculation? We prefer a short amendment we can sign (DocuSign) and a short ops runbook so our SREs know fallback behaviors.

Appreciate a quick timeline — we have a board-readout on 2025-07-24.

Best,
Sara
Director of Engineering, Atlas Biomed

Thanks for the ping. High-level technical proposal below — keeping it conservative so we don't expose other tenants or weaken isolation guarantees.

1) Conditional soft-headroom window
- Trigger: sustained 30%+ qps above Atlas baseline for a 3-minute rolling window.
- Behavior: provision soft-headroom by keeping up to 2 GPUs in warm-standby (no hard isolation, reclaimed after 10 minutes idle). This avoids preemption spikes but is limited to customers with committed pools >=8 GPUs.
- Limits: max 10 minutes per event, 120 minutes per month; tagged as non-guaranteed burst (observable in console).

2) Deterministic fallback path
- On queue depth crossing threshold or priority preemption, route new requests to pre-approved quantized model variant (same weights, lower precision) with explicit outbound header for customer observability.
- KV cache warming: warn customers that cold KV warms may add initial latency; include a prefetch step in playbook.

3) Crediting calculation (suggested)
- Credit minutes = sum_over_incidents(max(0, degraded_minutes - 2)) to allow two nuisance minutes per month.
- Credit amount = (Credit minutes / total_committed_minutes) * monthly_reserved_fee * 0.5 (50% weight — partial credit because fallback preserves availability). Example attached in sheet.

4) Ops runbook summary (for playbook doc)
- On alert: 1) verify metrics (qps, queue depth, preemption logs), 2) flip to fallback model variant for user-facing endpoints, 3) enable soft-headroom if thresholds met, 4) page Redwood infra if anomalies persist > 15 minutes.

I attached a short PDF playbook and a sample credit calculation spreadsheet. Please review and let me know what commercial language you want to pair with this.

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — thanks for the patience while we drafted this.

Attached are two items: 1) a concise operations playbook (PDF) that walks through the detection and fallback steps, and 2) a proposed SLA amendment draft that codifies the conditional soft-headroom and a deterministic crediting formula. Highlights:
- Soft-headroom: available to customers with >=8 GPUs; auto-activated based on 30%+ sustained qps delta and capped at 10 minutes per event.
- Fallback model: we will route to your pre-approved quantized variant for degraded requests; we include an outbound header so you can monitor which responses used the fallback path.
- Crediting: first 2 nuisance minutes per month are excluded; remaining degraded minutes are credited pro rata as 50% of reserved fee proportional to time.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached SLA amendment draft ("sla_amendment_draft.docx") and the playbook PDF.
2) If acceptable, I'll push the DocuSign envelope (we've added a HubSpot deal record: ATB-98765).
3) If you want any operational adjustments (e.g., shorter trigger window or lower max minutes), propose the numbers and we can iterate quickly.

We can also schedule a 30-minute call with Ben (solutions) and David (infra) if your SREs want to walk through the runbook.

Would you like us to send the DocuSign package by end of day tomorrow?

Best,
Rachel Kim
